extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing reciprocal exclusion from practice before the USPTO based on a state-court disbarment and describing the procedural steps, findings, and relief ordered. Targets enforcement/disciplinary context for patent practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a state authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order filed requested that the Director impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the Supreme Court of the State of Colorado in The People of the State of Colorado vs. Glenn L. Webb. Action taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exclusion: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1)/(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was excluded for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (specifically § 11.804(h)(1)), predicated upon being disbarred from the practice of law on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice states the exclusion is predicated on Respondent's disbarment by the State of Colorado; the Final Order adopts that predicate as the basis for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure: Notice and opportunity to respond (mailing and 40-day response)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be mailed (here by certified mail) and provide the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed (certified mail receipt noted). The Notice informed Respondent of the 40-day response opportunity and the statutory grounds under § 11.24(d)(1) to oppose identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond: no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was returned undeliverable and was subsequently published in the Official Gazette; Respondent did not file a response, and the Final Order determines there is no genuine issue of material fact and imposes exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication as alternative notice (Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: If mailed notice is returned undeliverable, publication in the Official Gazette may be used; the Notice and Order in this case was published and no response was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was returned as undeliverable on February 20, 2015, and was subsequently published in the Official Gazette. Publication was treated as sufficient for proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive misconduct findings supporting discipline (abandonment and communication failures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state court found Respondent abandoned and failed to adequately communicate with three clients, violating professional responsibility rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Opinion and Decision cited client abandonment and inadequate communication as bases for discipline; these conduct types are recognized bases for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive misconduct findings supporting discipline (conversion of client funds / failure to pay USPTO fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: While representing two clients, Respondent accepted money to pay patent-related fees but never paid the fees to the USPTO, thereby engaging in conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion of client funds intended for patent-related fees was a key factual basis for the Colorado court's disbarment and supports reciprocal exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive misconduct findings supporting discipline (misrepresentations to clients)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state court held that Respondent lied to two clients about the status of their patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing misrepresentations to clients about case status are a basis for disciplinary action and were cited by the Colorado decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable state professional conduct rules violated
rubrics_metrics.description: The Colorado court found violations of Colo. RPC 1.1, 1.3, 1.4(a)(3), 1.16(d), 8.1(b), and 8.4(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order identifies the specific state rules that the respondent's conduct violated; those rule violations formed the basis for the state disbarment and thus for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief: exclusion from practice before USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly commands exclusion from all USPTO practice areas (patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters) as the primary disciplinary sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Exclusion content and form
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette identifying the respondent, registration number, the nature of the sanction, and the predicate state action and findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a model 'NOTICE OF EXCLUSION' that discloses the respondent's name, residence, registration number, the state disbarment and the factual bases (abandonment, conversion, misrepresentations), and cites the regulations under which action was taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires transmission of disciplinary notice to state agencies and courts as specified by § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of excluded practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires compliance with § 11.58 but does not restate the duties; compliance with those enumerated duties is a condition of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissociation is ordered as a remedial step to prevent the excluded practitioner's continued electronic or client-linked practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative bar on use of USPTO customer accounts or access until formal reinstatement to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of disciplinary decisions (OED Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes that disciplinary decisions are made publicly accessible via the OED Reading Room, providing transparency and public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residual/other relief clause
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may order 'such other and further relief as the nature of this cause shall require.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order reserves authority to impose additional remedial measures beyond those explicitly listed if warranted by the circumstances.
